key_insight: A graph neural network can accurately predict transition-metal adsorption energies on graphene quantum dots, enabling rapid screening of single-atom catalyst candidates.
engineering_relevance: This cuts the cost of first-principles exploration by about six orders of magnitude, making catalyst discovery on carbon nanostructures far more scalable.
method: Trained a GNN on DFT-generated adsorption-energy data for transition metals on graphene quantum dots.
Used graph-based molecular/atomic structure representation to learn adsorption trends.
Applied the model for fast prediction of new adsorption configurations.
evidence_signal: The model achieved R² = 0.906 and MAE = 0.101 eV on the reported evaluation, while reducing computational cost by roughly six orders of magnitude versus DFT.
watch_item: Performance is tied to the DFT training distribution, so predictions may be less reliable for unseen metal–surface motifs or GQD chemistries outside the training set.
paper_title: GQD-AdsNet: Graph Neural Networks Unlock Rapid Exploration of Transition Metal Adsorption on Graphene Quantum Dots
